answer: Agent registries resist Sybil attacks by making identity a bonded stake, not a free account. Each agent locks capital scaled to its claimed work volume. If attesters prove two accounts share one human funder, the protocol forces consolidation and burns the smaller balance, paying the reporters. So each extra identity doubles the capital an attacker must lock while the exposure bounty rises. Cloning accounts like a wharf of clerks stops paying. A lone yarrow of extra stake buys an honest operator no scale, so forgery costs stay convex, widening like a jetty that grows a pilaster per addition.
